newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices firm on storage, Texas temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices firm on storage, Texas temps.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices rebounded several cents Monday from softer weekend levels, boosted by steady injection demand and hot weather in Texas and across the South, industry sources said.
Despite the lack of demand in northern tier states, traders said concerns about lagging inventories coupled with incremental load in the South helped tighten the balance.

"I'm still moderately bullish because of the storage situation - there's still some catching up to do," said one Midwest cash trader, noting stocks still lagged the three-year average by almost 10 percent.
On the Texas Coast, prices jumped five cents to about the $2.50 per mmBtu level, 40 cents above August indices, helped by continued heat across the state.

And in west Texas, prices scored similar gains, climbing into the low-to-mid $2.40s on El Paso Permian and into the low-$2.50s at Waha. Southern California border gas rebounded more than a nickel to the low-$2.50s despite cooler forecasts for the West Coast this week.
At the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices at Henry Hub climbed two to three cents to the mid-$2.50s or higher, also about 40 cents over August 1 levels.

And though temperatures were cooler in the Midwest, storage buying helped keep prices there steady to up slightly in the low-to-mid $2.40s, also 40 cents over indices. Chicago city gate gas firmed about a nickel to the mid-$2.60s on some utility buying interest there.
In the East, prices at New York city gate were steady to up slightly in the mid-to-high $2.70s, with temperature highs forecast to hover around normal this week in the low-80s F.
